Thanks Marissa — we’ll take point on legal. High-level plan and turnaround below: 

1) Upon receipt of Acme redlines (target 2026-03-09 EOD):
   - Redwood legal (me) will produce a counter-redline (track changes) to the MSA within 2 business days (target: 2026-03-11).
   - I’ll mark any non-standard commercial requests and propose fallback language.

2) DPA: Redwood will provide our standard DPA template within 3 business days of receiving Acme comments (target: 2026-03-12).

3) SLA:
   - Dev (Dev Patel) will own SLA metric language (availability, latency, incident response) and provide proposed wording + verification plan within 3 business days after seeing Acme redlines.
   - Legal will review SLA edits for contractual consistency (1 business day review).

4) Escalation / negotiation owners:
   - Legal (Neha) handles commercial/legal term negotiations (indemnities, liability caps, data treatment).
   - Product/Infra (Dev) handles technical SLO disagreements and measurement.
   - Marissa will coordinate weekly syncs and keep MAP updated.

5) Turnaround expectations:
   - Legal review turnaround: 1-2 business days for standard sections; longer if we need policy/finance sign-off.
   - Product turnaround for SLA edits: 2-3 business days depending on scope.

6) Target close date: 2026-03-16 (aligns with procurement windows). If Acme misses the 3/9 redline date, we’ll push target close by one week.

I’m attaching our working countertrack and the DPA template so everyone has the starting point.
